Con una esfera y un suelo se ve; para mo: With a sphere and a floor you can see; to model you need a workshop. The smooth minimum is a [[gfx-decidir|mix]] with a parabolic pinch, the repetition is the grid's [[gfx-repetir|mod]] taken to three dimensions, and twisting is rotating with an angle that depends on the height.
En el tema de [[gfx-raymarching|raymarch: In the [[gfx-raymarching|raymarching]] topic you put together a sphere and a floor. With that you can already see in three dimensions, but you cannot model: to build something worth looking at you need a few more tools, and they are all of the same family. This topic is the workshop, and it is worth coming back to when you are making your own things.
La unión de dos cuerpos es <code>min(a,: The union of two bodies is min(a, b), and it works: but the result has a hard edge where the two surfaces cross, like two stones glued together. Nature almost never does that. Two drops that meet form a smooth neck, and a branch leaves the trunk with a widening.
La solución es una versión suavizada del: The solution is a smoothed version of the minimum:
\\operatorname{smin}(a, b, k) = \\operat: \operatorname{smin}(a, b, k) = \operatorname{mix}(b,\ a,\ h) \;-\; k\,h\,(1 - h)
La primera línea es un $h$ que vale 1 cu: The first line is an $h$ that is 1 when $a$ clearly wins, 0 when $b$ wins, and something in between in the band of width $k$ where they are tying. The second interpolates between the two values and also subtracts a pinch: that $-k\,h(1-h)$ is a parabola that is zero at the extremes and $k/4$ at the centre, and it is exactly what creates the neck.
Un punto está a $0{,}1$ de las dos esfer: A point is $0{.}1$ from both spheres at once, $a = b = 0{.}1$, with $k = 0{.}4$. Does the smooth minimum give more or less than the ordinary minimum?
Con $a = b$, $h = \\frac{1}{2}$ y el pel: With $a = b$, $h = \frac{1}{2}$ and the pinch is $k/4 = 0{.}1$: $\operatorname{smin} = 0{.}1 - 0{.}1 = 0$. The point is right on the neck's surface, even though it is 0.1 from each sphere. Matter has been created there.
Serían iguales lejos de la zona de fusió: They would be equal far from the fusion zone. Right where they tie is where the subtraction is greatest: it is the definition of the neck.
Más: el suavizado aleja la superficie: More: the smoothing moves the surface away
Al revés: el pellizco se resta. La super: The other way round: the pinch is subtracted. The surface comes closer to the point, that is, the bodies swell towards each other.

Two spheres that come closer and move apart. The k control is the width of the fusion: at zero it is an ordinary min and they cross like two stones; raise it and they behave like mercury.

El <code>smin</code> tiene un precio: el: The smin has a price: the result is no longer an exact distance, but a bound that is sometimes over-optimistic. In practice it shows little, but if you raise $k$ a lot artefacts start to appear, and the solution is to advance prudently: t += h * 0.7 instead of t += h.
Con el mínimo suave y sus parientes, la: With the smooth minimum and its relatives, the list of operations that serve for modelling is short and can be learned by heart:
inflar el cuerpo $r$ en todas direccione: inflating the body by $r$ in all directions: round corners
quedarse solo con una capa de grosor $2t: keeping only a layer of thickness $2t$ around the surface
Las dos últimas líneas son las que más j: The last two rows are the ones that give most play. abs(d) - t turns any body into its own hollow shell, because abs makes the inside “far” again. And adding a sine to the distance pushes the surface in and out, which is real relief, not the fake one of the derivatives topic: here the silhouette changes too.

La repetición del tema de la [[gfx-repet: The repetition of the [[gfx-repetir|grid]] topic works just the same in three dimensions, and there it really does impress: a single column, and suddenly there are infinitely many.
Con el mismo aviso de siempre, ahora más: With the usual warning, now graver: the figure has to fit comfortably in its cell. If it spills out, the ray cuts it, because it never looks at the neighbouring cell. And if you want a finite number of copies, you limit the cell index instead of the space:
Una columna, un suelo, una repetición y: One column, a floor, a repetition and a twist. Everything you see fits in fifteen lines and there is not one object stored in memory. Move the twist slowly.
Con torsión 0 las columnas son rectas. C: With twist 0 the columns are straight. With 0.3, will they all twist the same, or will those far from the centre lean more than the near ones? Think about what turns: the whole plane.

La línea de la torsión, <code>q.xz = gir: The twist's line, q.xz = giro(torsion * q.y) * q.xz, is a rotation whose angle depends on the height. With that a straight column becomes a barley-sugar column, and nothing has had to be modelled.
Al torcer, escalar de forma desigual o s: On twisting, scaling unevenly or adding relief, the function stops returning the true distance and returns something greater in some places. That is where the rays skip over the surface and holes appear. Practical rule: if you have twisted or deformed, multiply the step by 0.5 or 0.7. It is the cheap way of recovering the guarantee.
Esta forma de modelar —describir un sóli: This way of modelling —describing a solid with a function instead of with a mesh— is called implicit modelling and is not only for artists. In 3D printing it makes it possible to generate internal structures (lattices, foams, density gradients) that would be impossible to draw vertex by vertex. In industrial design, changing one parameter remakes the whole part without fixing broken meshes. In medicine, the surfaces extracted from a CT scan are scalar fields with a threshold, which is exactly this. And there are free programs, like Fragmentarium or Blender itself with its nodes, that work this way.
Jim Blinn describió las «gotas» (<em>blo: Jim Blinn described “blobs” (blobby models) in 1982 while looking for how to draw molecules without their looking like billiard balls glued together, and out of that came the whole family of implicit surfaces. The particular smin you are using, the polynomial version, was popularised by Íñigo Quílez forty years later, and its charm is that it has neither a root nor an exponential: two products and an interpolation.
El smin devuelve menos que la distancia: The smin returns less than the real distance in the fusion zone: the ray can overshoot. With $k$ large, advance with t += 0.7 * h.
